title: Childhood, schooling and violin lessons with Dave Perkins
summary: Born in Donaldsonville, moved to New Orleans, church and school, studied violin with Professor Dave Perkins.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: How did you, you were, how many years in Donaldsonville? Only about seven.
No, I was born in the house of the house. Yeah. Half the band, just children born and all about half born in the audience. Uh-huh.
How old were you when you moved?

Oh, I was almost a young boy. I remember going to kindergarten school, and I remember going to the only public school I had for blacks, out at the end of River Avenue. And when we come to New Orleans, we move on, and Boydhead and Oak, I was going to the, we could call it the, the church on the side of Cowden Avenue, it's still there, but they called it something else. That's where I made my first communion, so I must have been very young. When you first? First communion, because I'm catechic, see, and conforming and everything. They did call it St. Dominic, but they didn't change the name of it, you see. And then we moved into the Garden District, because I went to Holy Ghost School. And then, that's where my daddy, like I said, sent me to the professor, Dave Perkins, to learn music and he decided I should learn violin. But all I got out of him was learn how to read music and everything.
Did you play any banjo before you went to the band?

No, how the banjo came about. My brother was working at the war lines, and he bought a banjo and I was teaching him, and he got discouraged with him, and I bought the banjo back from him. I bought him. And I taught myself the banjo. And the guitar, I taught myself for a reason, because I had already learned music through playing the violin, you see. You could do those things.
